# Text that looks like a comment and is read by a tool

Read the sections for the languages in the repository before pruning. The lists are not complete, so the recognition rules come first: they are what protects a directive you have never seen.

Keeping a comment that turned out to be plain prose costs one line. Deleting one that a tool reads can change a build, a test result, or the program's output. When unsure, keep it.

## Recognition rules

1. **Position.** Anything on the first two lines of a file, or in the leading comment block before the first code, may be a directive: shebangs, encoding lines, license identifiers, parser and type-checker switches. So may a comment that must sit directly on, above, or below the line it affects.
2. **Shape.** A comment is a directive when it begins with a tool name followed by a colon, a hyphen and a verb, or an equals sign (`//go:`, `# noqa:`, `// eslint-disable`, `# shellcheck disable=`), or when its first word is one of `ignore`, `disable`, `enable`, `skip`, `off`, `on`, `suppress`, `expect`, `pragma`, `keep`, `nolint`, `noqa`, `nosec`. Spacing is part of the syntax: some tools need `//nolint` with no space, others `// NOLINT` with one. Do not reflow, reword, or move these.
3. **Sigils.** A comment marker followed immediately by a punctuation character is usually a contract: `#!`, `#:`, `#|`, `#[`, `///`, `//!`, `//#`, `//~`, `//@`, `/*!`, `/*+`, `/*#`, `/*@`, `<!--#`, `<!--[`, `-- +`, `--%`.
4. **Pairs.** Markers that open and close a region are one unit: `begin`/`end`, `start`/`stop`, `off`/`on`, `disable`/`enable`, `push`/`pop`, `region`/`endregion`, `tag::`/`end::`. Never remove one half, and never edit a generator-owned region between them by hand.
5. **Reasons and expiry.** Text after a suppression (`-- reason`, `// reason`, `: reason`, `exp:2026-01-01`) belongs to the directive. Some tools reject a suppression without it.
6. **Test oracles.** In test files and fixtures, a comment can be the expected result: expected output, expected diagnostics, commands to run. It goes only when the test goes.
7. **Consumed documentation.** A docstring or doc comment is program data when code or a generator reads it: command-line help, API schemas, tool descriptions shown to a model, generated reference pages, bindings. Search for the reader (`__doc__`, a derive macro, a docs generator in the build) before trimming.
8. **Doc gates.** If the project turns missing documentation into an error, removing a public doc comment fails the build. Check the lint configuration first.
9. **Generated files.** A file marked as generated (`Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT`, `@generated`, `<auto-generated>`, `Generated by`) belongs to its generator. Change nothing in it.
10. **Not comments at all.** Some syntax only resembles a comment: PHP attributes `#[...]`, `'use client'` and `'use strict'` strings, C `#pragma` and `#line`, C# `#nullable` and `#region`, `#cmakedefine` in templates, a `#` inside a string, heredoc, or YAML block scalar, SQL `COMMENT ON`, GraphQL `"""descriptions"""`.

To check a suspected suppression, use the linter's own report of unused directives where it has one (Ruff `RUF100`, mypy `warn_unused_ignores`, ESLint `--report-unused-disable-directives`, PHPStan `reportUnmatchedIgnoredErrors`, staticcheck, Biome, Deno `ban-unused-ignore`). Do not decide by reading.

## Every language

- License and copyright headers, `SPDX-License-Identifier:`, `SPDX-FileCopyrightText:`. In JavaScript and CSS, `/*! ... */`, `@license`, and `@preserve` survive minifiers on purpose.
- Shebang on line 1. Editor modelines (`vim:`, `-*- mode -*-`).
- Generated-file markers and generator-owned regions: `<!-- BEGIN_TF_DOCS -->`, `<!-- START doctoc -->`, `<!-- ALL-CONTRIBUTORS-LIST:START -->`, `[[[cog ... ]]]`, `# >>> conda initialize >>>`.
- Documentation include markers: `// tag::name[]` / `// end::name[]` (Asciidoctor), `// ANCHOR: name` / `// ANCHOR_END: name` (mdBook), `{@snippet}` markup (`// @start region=`, `// @highlight`).
- Dependency-bot hints: `# renovate: datasource=... depName=...`.
- Secret and security scanners: `# nosec`, `#nosec G101 -- why`, `# nosemgrep: rule`, `# pragma: allowlist secret`, `//NOSONAR`.
- Translator comments extracted into message catalogs: `# Translators:`, `// TRANSLATORS:`, `/* translators: */`.
- `// Deprecated:` paragraphs and `@deprecated` tags, which tools and compilers act on.

## Python

- Line 1 or 2: `# -*- coding: ... -*-`. Inline script metadata block `# /// script` to `# ///`.
- Types: `# type: ignore[code]`, `# type: int` type comments, `# mypy: ...`, `# pyright: ...`, `# pyre-ignore`, `# pytype: disable=`.
- Lint and format: `# noqa`, `# noqa: CODE`, `# ruff: noqa`, `# flake8: noqa`, `# pylint: disable=`, `# isort: skip`, `# isort: off`/`on`, `# fmt: off`/`on`/`skip`.
- Coverage: `# pragma: no cover`, `# pragma: no branch`.
- Doctests: `>>>` examples and their expected output in docstrings, `# doctest: +ELLIPSIS`.
- Docstrings read at run time: `argparse` with `description=__doc__`, click and typer command help, docopt usage grammar, Fire, FastAPI route descriptions, DRF and Django admin, pydantic `use_attribute_docstrings`, tool decorators that turn a docstring into a model-facing description. Sphinx autodoc, napoleon sections, mkdocstrings, and `#:` attribute comments feed generated docs.
- Notebooks as scripts: `# %%` cells, `#| option:` (Quarto), `# Databricks notebook source`, `# COMMAND ----------`.
- Cython: `# cython: ...`, `# distutils: ...`.

## JavaScript and TypeScript

- File top: `// @ts-check`, `// @ts-nocheck`, `/// <reference ... />`, `// @flow`, `/** @jest-environment jsdom */`, `// @vitest-environment`, `/** @jsx h */`, `/** @jsxImportSource x */`.
- Types: `// @ts-expect-error`, `// @ts-ignore`, `// $FlowFixMe[code]`. In projects that type-check JavaScript, JSDoc tags are the types: `@type`, `@param`, `@returns`, `@typedef`, `@template`, `@satisfies`. `@internal` with `stripInternal`, and API Extractor release tags `@public`, `@beta`, `@alpha`. Closure Compiler annotations.
- Lint and format: `eslint-disable`, `eslint-disable-next-line rule -- reason`, `/* eslint rule: "error" */`, `/* global name */`, `// prettier-ignore`, `// biome-ignore lint/x/y: reason`, `// deno-lint-ignore`.
- Coverage: `/* istanbul ignore next */`, `/* c8 ignore start */`/`stop`, `/* v8 ignore next */`.
- Bundlers: `/* webpackChunkName: "x" */` and the other `webpack*` comments inside `import()`, `/* @vite-ignore */`, `/* turbopackIgnore: true */`, `/* @__PURE__ */`, `/* #__PURE__ */`, `/*#__NO_SIDE_EFFECTS__*/`, `//# sourceMappingURL=`, `//# sourceURL=`.
- Type tests and doc samples: `// $ExpectType`, `// $ExpectError`, `// ^?`, `// @errors:`, `// ---cut---`.

## Go

- `//go:build`, `// +build`, `//go:generate`, `//go:embed`, `//go:linkname`, `//go:noinline` and the other `//go:` pragmas, `//go:debug`, `//line`, `//export`.
- The comment directly above `import "C"` is C code, including its `#cgo` lines.
- `//nolint:name // reason`, `//lint:ignore Check reason`, `//lint:file-ignore`, `//revive:disable`, `// #nosec`.
- Tests: `// Output:` and `// Unordered output:` in `Example` functions, `// want "regexp"` in analyzer test data.
- Generators: swag `// @Summary`, `// @Param`, `// @Router`; `// @gotags:` in `.proto` files; comments in `.proto` files flow into generated code.

## Rust

- `///` and `//!` are `#[doc]` attributes, visible to macros. Derives turn them into output: clap help text, schemars and utoipa schema descriptions, strum messages, pyo3 `__doc__`, cbindgen annotations (`/// cbindgen:ignore`).
- Code blocks in doc comments are tests. Fence attributes (`no_run`, `ignore`, `should_panic`, `compile_fail`) and hidden lines starting with `# ` are part of them. `#![doc = include_str!("../README.md")]` makes README code blocks tests too.
- `// SAFETY:` above an `unsafe` block, and `# Safety`, `# Errors`, `# Panics` headings, are required by Clippy lints when enabled.
- `#![deny(missing_docs)]` or `#![warn(missing_docs)]` with warnings denied makes every public doc comment mandatory.
- Compiler test suites: `//~ ERROR`, `//@ compile-flags:`, and neighbouring `.stderr` files.

## C and C++

- `/* FALLTHROUGH */` and its spellings, which GCC matches by pattern.
- `// NOLINT(check)`, `// NOLINTNEXTLINE`, `// NOLINTBEGIN`/`END`, `// clang-format off`/`on`, `// cppcheck-suppress id`, `//-V501`, `// IWYU pragma: keep` and the other IWYU pragmas, `coverity[...]` annotations.
- Doxygen commands that change what is emitted: `\cond`/`\endcond`, `@{`/`@}`, `\internal`, `\defgroup`. kernel-doc `/** name() - ... */` blocks.
- Test suites: `// RUN:`, `// REQUIRES:`, `// CHECK:` and `CHECK-*:`, `// expected-error {{...}}`, `/* { dg-error "..." } */`.

## Java and Kotlin

- Javadoc with doclint enabled; `@deprecated` paired with `@Deprecated`.
- `// CHECKSTYLE:OFF`/`ON`, `// SUPPRESS CHECKSTYLE Name`, `// NOPMD`, `// spotless:off`/`on`, `// @formatter:off`/`on`, `//noinspection Name`, `//$NON-NLS-1$`.
- Maven plugin Javadoc tags (`@goal`, `@parameter`) in older plugins.
- KDoc `@sample` pulls in a named function's body. Dokka `reportUndocumented` with `failOnWarning` is the Kotlin doc gate.

## C#

- `///` XML docs feed IntelliSense, DocFX, and Swagger descriptions (`IncludeXmlComments`). With a documentation file enabled and warnings as errors, CS1591 makes them mandatory, and CS1574 checks `cref` targets.
- `// ReSharper disable Name`/`restore`, `// <auto-generated>`.
- File-based apps: `#:package`, `#:sdk`, `#:property` lines at the top.

## Swift

- `// swift-tools-version:` on line 1 of `Package.swift`.
- `// swiftlint:disable rule`/`enable`/`:next`/`:previous`, `// swiftformat:disable`, `// swift-format-ignore`.
- `// MARK:` drives editor navigation; keep it where the project uses it.

## Ruby and PHP

- Ruby: `# frozen_string_literal: true`, `# encoding:`, `# typed: strict` (Sorbet), `#: (String) -> Integer` and `# @rbs` (RBS inline), `# @type var` and `# steep:ignore` (Steep), `# rubocop:disable Cop -- reason`/`enable`/`todo`, `# :nodoc:`, YARD tags. Text after `__END__` is data.
- PHP: `// phpcs:ignore`, `// phpcs:disable`/`enable`, `@phpstan-ignore`, `@psalm-suppress`, `@codeCoverageIgnore`, `@SuppressWarnings(PHPMD.x)`. PHPDoc types are read by PHPStan and Psalm. Doctrine `@ORM\` annotations and other docblock annotations are configuration. WordPress plugin and theme header comments register the plugin or theme.

## Shell, Dockerfile, infrastructure

- Shell: `# shellcheck disable=SC0000`, `# shellcheck source=path`, `# shellcheck shell=sh`, `# bats test_tags=`.
- Dockerfile: `# syntax=`, `# escape=`, `# check=` at the top; `# hadolint ignore=DL0000`.
- Terraform and friends: `#trivy:ignore:rule`, `#tfsec:ignore:rule`, `#checkov:skip=ID:reason`, `# tflint-ignore: rule`, `# kics-scan ignore`.
- YAML: `# yaml-language-server: $schema=`, `# yamllint disable`, helm-docs `# -- description`, `# @schema` blocks, `#cloud-config` on line 1, `# noqa` for ansible-lint. TOML: `#:schema`.
- CMake and Bazel: `# cmake-lint: disable=`, `# cmake-format: off`/`on`, `# buildifier: disable=`, `# keep`, `# gazelle:` directives.
- Makefile: `## description` after a target, where a `help` target prints them.

## SQL

- Migration and query tools: `-- name: GetUser :one` (sqlc), `-- +goose Up`/`Down`/`StatementBegin`, `-- migrate:up`/`down` (dbmate), `-- +migrate Up` (sql-migrate), `--liquibase formatted sql`, `--changeset author:id`, `--rollback`.
- Executed by the database: optimizer hints `/*+ ... */`, MySQL `/*! ... */` and `/*!50110 ... */`.
- `-- noqa` and `-- noqa: disable=rule` (sqlfluff).

## CSS, HTML, templates, Markdown

- CSS: `/* stylelint-disable */` and its variants, `/* autoprefixer: off */`, `/* prettier-ignore */`, `/* @noflip */`.
- HTML: conditional comments `<!--[if mso]>`, server-side includes `<!--# include -->`, `<!--esi -->`, WordPress block delimiters `<!-- wp:name -->`, `<!-- svelte-ignore code -->`, `<!-- htmlmin:ignore -->`, Thymeleaf `<!--/*/ ... /*/-->`.
- Markdown: front matter between `---` lines, `<!-- markdownlint-disable -->` and its variants, `<!-- prettier-ignore-start -->`/`end`, `<!-- vale off -->`/`on`, `<!--more-->` and `<!-- truncate -->` excerpt markers, table-of-contents markers, and code-fence info strings that a doc-test runner reads.

## Other languages

The same hazard exists wherever a tool reads comments: R roxygen `#'`, Emacs Lisp `;;;###autoload`, Lua `---@` annotations, Haskell Haddock `-- |` and `{-# PRAGMA #-}`, Perl `## no critic` and POD, PowerShell comment-based help (`<# .SYNOPSIS #>`) and `#requires`, LaTeX `% !TEX`. Apply the recognition rules.
